jp: 来月[らいげつ]、京都[きょうと]へ行[い]く{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I intend to go to Kyoto next month.
why: Your own intention to do something is a verb in dictionary form plus つもり.

jp: 今日[きょう]は早[はや]く寝[ね]る{つもりだ|pt-tsumori}。
en: I intend to go to bed early today.
why: A speaker's own plan or resolve is stated with つもり after the dictionary form.

jp: 大学[だいがく]を出[で]たら、日本[にほん]で働[はたら]く{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: After I graduate, I plan to work in Japan.
why: The speaker's own plan for the future takes つもり.

jp: 田中[たなか]さんの誕生日[たんじょうび]に、花[はな]をあげる{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I plan to give Mr. Tanaka flowers for his birthday.
why: What the speaker has in mind to do is expressed with つもり.

jp: お酒[さけ]はもう飲[の]まない{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I intend not to drink alcohol any more.
why: A negative intention is the negative plain form plus つもり: ないつもり.

jp: 彼[かれ]に謝[あやま]る{つもりはありません|pt-tsumori}。
en: I have no intention of apologizing to him.
why: つもりはありません flatly denies any intention to do something.

jp: 今年[ことし]の夏[なつ]は海[うみ]へ行[い]く{つもりでした|pt-tsumori}が、仕事[しごと]が忙[いそが]しくて行[い]けませんでした。
en: I had intended to go to the sea this summer, but I was too busy at work and couldn't.
why: A past intention that did not come about is つもりでした followed by が.

jp: 外食[がいしょく]した{つもりで|pt-tsumori}、その分[ぶん]のお金[かね]を貯金[ちょきん]します。
en: I'll put that money into savings as if I had eaten out.
why: A past-form verb plus つもりで means acting as if something had happened.

jp: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]でも、走[はし]る{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: Even if it rains tomorrow, I intend to run.
why: The speaker's firm intention despite the weather is つもりです.

jp: 結婚[けっこん]しても、この仕事[しごと]を続[つづ]ける{つもりだ|pt-tsumori}。
en: Even after I marry, I intend to keep this job.
why: A resolution about one's own future uses plain form plus つもりだ.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]みに、友達[ともだち]と富士山[ふじさん]に登[のぼ]る{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I plan to climb Mt. Fuji with friends in the summer holidays.
why: A plan the speaker has made for the holidays takes つもり.

jp: 母[はは]の日[ひ]には、母[はは]に手紙[てがみ]を書[か]く{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: On Mother's Day I intend to write my mother a letter.
why: What the speaker means to do is a dictionary-form verb plus つもり.

jp: 来年[らいねん]から、毎朝[まいあさ]ジョギングを始[はじ]める{つもりだ|pt-tsumori}。
en: I intend to start jogging every morning from next year.
why: A decision about one's own future behaviour is expressed with つもりだ.

jp: 冗談[じょうだん]{のつもりで|pt-tsumori}言[い]ったのですが、彼女[かのじょ]を怒[おこ]らせてしまいました。
en: I said it meaning it as a joke, but I ended up making her angry.
why: Noun plus のつもりで says what the speaker meant something to be.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]の会議[かいぎ]には出席[しゅっせき]する{つもりです|pt-tsumori}が、少[すこ]し遅[おく]れるかもしれません。
en: I intend to attend next week's meeting, but I may be a little late.
why: The speaker states a personal intention before adding a caveat, so つもり fits.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]みはどうするのかと聞[き]かれて、国[くに]へ帰[かえ]る{つもりだ|pt-tsumori}と答[こた]えた。
en: When I was asked what I was doing in the summer holidays, I answered that I planned to go back to my country.
why: The speaker reports their own answer about their plan, so つもりだ; そうだ would be hearsay.

jp: 今度[こんど]の試験[しけん]では、絶対[ぜったい]に合格[ごうかく]する{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I fully intend to pass the next exam.
why: A strong personal resolve about the speaker's own goal takes つもりです.

jp: 田中[たなか]さんは、来年[らいねん]会社[かいしゃ]を辞[や]める{つもりだ|pt-tsumori}と言[い]っていました。
en: Mr. Tanaka said he intends to quit the company next year.
why: つもりだ also reports another person's stated intention, here quoted with と.

jp: 誰[だれ]に何[なん]と言[い]われても、この仕事[しごと]を辞[や]める{つもりはない|pt-tsumori}。
en: No matter what anyone says to me, I have no intention of quitting this job.
why: Refusing to do something of one's own will is つもりはない.

jp: 今夜[こんや]は家[いえ]で晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を作[つく]る{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I'm planning to cook dinner at home tonight.
why: The speaker's plan for the evening is a dictionary-form verb plus つもり.

jp: 私[わたし]たちは三年間[さんねんかん]、日本[にほん]に住[す]む{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: We intend to live in Japan for three years.
why: A plan made by the speakers themselves takes つもりです.

jp: 風邪[かぜ]を引[ひ]いたので、今日[きょう]は会社[かいしゃ]を休[やす]む{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I've caught a cold, so I intend to take the day off work today.
why: The speaker's decision to stay home is expressed with つもり.

jp: 父[ちち]の誕生日[たんじょうび]に、新[あたら]しい時計[とけい]をプレゼントする{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I plan to give my father a new watch for his birthday.
why: A plan to do something for someone is the dictionary form plus つもり.

jp: 将来[しょうらい]は、小[ちい]さい店[みせ]を開[ひら]く{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: In the future I intend to open a small shop.
why: A long-term personal aim is stated with つもり.

jp: 約束[やくそく]したので、今日[きょう]は残業[ざんぎょう]しない{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I made a promise, so I intend not to work overtime today.
why: A negative intention is the plain negative form plus つもり.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]の旅行[りょこう]には、カメラを持[も]っていく{つもりだ|pt-tsumori}。
en: I plan to take my camera on next week's trip.
why: The speaker says what they plan to bring, so the sentence ends in つもりだ.

jp: 甘[あま]い物[もの]は食[た]べない{つもりだった|pt-tsumori}のに、ケーキを二[ふた]つも食[た]べてしまった。
en: I had meant not to eat sweet things, yet I ended up eating two pieces of cake.
why: A past intention contradicted by what happened is つもりだった followed by のに.

jp: 母[はは]に電話[でんわ]する{つもりでしたが|pt-tsumori}、忘[わす]れてしまいました。
en: I meant to phone my mother, but I forgot.
why: An earlier intention that was not carried out is つもりでしたが.

jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]は部屋[へや]を掃除[そうじ]する{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I'm planning to clean my room this weekend.
why: The speaker's plan for the weekend takes つもり.

jp: 彼[かれ]とは、もう二度[にど]と会[あ]わない{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I intend never to see him again.
why: A firm negative resolve is the negative plain form plus つもり.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]三十分[さんじゅっぷん]、日本語[にほんご]を勉強[べんきょう]する{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I intend to study Japanese for thirty minutes every day.
why: The speaker's own study plan is expressed with つもり.

jp: 兄[あに]は大学院[だいがくいん]に進[すす]む{つもりだ|pt-tsumori}と言[い]っています。
en: My brother says he intends to go on to graduate school.
why: A person's own stated plan reported with と言う uses つもりだ.

jp: 今度[こんど]の日曜日[にちようび]は、どこにも行[い]かない{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: I don't plan to go anywhere this coming Sunday.
why: A negative plan uses the negative plain form plus つもり.

jp: 日本[にほん]で車[くるま]を買[か]う{つもりはありません|pt-tsumori}が、自転車[じてんしゃ]は買[か]いたいです。
en: I have no intention of buying a car in Japan, but I'd like to buy a bicycle.
why: Denying one's own intention is つもりはありません.

jp: 卒業[そつぎょう]してから、留学[りゅうがく]する{つもりです|pt-tsumori}。
en: After I graduate, I intend to study abroad.
why: An intended future step is stated with つもりです.
